title.en: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists guilty in national security trial
title.zh: 香港天安门活动人士在国家安全审判中被判有罪

summary.en: Three activists in Hong Kong have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under a national security law introduced by China.
summary.zh: 香港的三名活动人士因煽动他人颠覆国家政权，根据中国实施的国家安全法被判有罪。

body.en:
Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under the city's controversial national security law.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail after being convicted under the China-introduced law. Sentencing is expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", according to a summary on Friday. Chow told the court in May the law itself was on trial.

Hong Kong used to be one of the only places in Chinese territory where people could gather to mark the deadly 1989 crackdown against pro-democracy protesters.

Authorities banned these gatherings in 2020, citing Covid-19 policies, but they have never resumed. This was also the year the national security law, which makes illegal a wider range of dissenting acts, officially came into force.

In mainland China, authorities have banned even oblique references to the 1989 crackdown.

The HKA was founded in May 1989 to support students holding pro-democracy rallies. Weeks later, the Communist Party crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square with troops and tanks. Estimates of the death toll range from a few hundred to many thousands.

Over the next three decades, HKA called on authorities to accept responsibility for the crackdown, free dissidents and introduce democratic reform.

Rights group Amnesty International has said the case "relies on vague, overly broad and arbitrary definitions of 'subversion'".

Sarah Brooks, Amnesty International's Deputy Regional Director, said Chow and Lee had "not committed any recognisable crime".

"Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan are prisoners of conscience who should never have been prosecuted in the first place. They must be released immediately and unconditionally", she added.

In a separate case, Chow was arrested in June 2021 for "inciting" the public to take part in that year's vigil and later found guilty.

However, Hong Kong's top court overturned that conviction in 2022 , with a judge ruling the police hadn't properly justified the vigil's ban.

Chow Hang-tung spoke to the BBC in 2021, weeks before her arrest on 4 June 2022.

Critics say the national security law has eroded Hong Kong's autonomy and created a climate of fear. Authorities insist it is needed to maintain stability.

Among other things, the law criminalises anything considered as secession, or breaking away from China; subversion; terrorism; and collusion with foreign or external forces.
body.zh: 根据香港备受争议的国家安全法，两名组织年度守夜活动纪念 1989 年天安门广场镇压活动的香港活动人士被判犯有煽动他人颠覆国家政权罪。 根据中国出台的法律，69岁的李卓人和41岁的周恒东被定罪，最高可判处10年监禁。预计将在晚些时候宣判。 根据周五的摘要，李和周“煽动他人以非法手段组织、策划、实施或者参与行为，以颠覆国家政权”。周五月份告诉法庭，该法律本身正在接受审判。 香港曾经是中国境内唯一一个人们可以聚集纪念1989年镇压亲民主抗议者的地方。 当局以 Covid-19 政策为由，在 2020 年禁止了这些聚会，但从未恢复。今年也是《国家安全法》正式生效的一年，该法将范围更广的异议行为定为非法。 在中国大陆，当局甚至禁止间接提及 1989 年的镇压行动。 香港学生会成立于1989年5月，旨在支持学生举行民主集会。几周后，共产党用军队和坦克镇压了北京天安门广场的民主抗议活动。死亡人数估计从数百人到数千人不等。 在接下来的三十年里，香港协会呼吁当局承担镇压责任，释放异见人士并推行民主改革。 人权组织国际特赦组织表示，此案“依赖于‘颠覆’的模糊、过于宽泛和武断的定义”。 国际特赦组织区域副主任萨拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 表示，周和李“没有犯下任何可识别的罪行”。 她补充说：“周恒东和李卓人是良心犯，本来就不应该受到起诉。必须立即无条件释放他们。” 在另一起案件中，周先生于 2021 年 6 月因“煽动”公众参加当年的守夜活动而被捕，后来被判有罪。 然而，香港最高法院于 2022 年推翻了这一判决，法官裁定警方没有适当证明禁止守夜活动的合理性。 周恒东于 2021 年接受 BBC 采访，几周后她于 2022 年 6 月 4 日被捕。 批评人士称，国家安全法削弱了香港的自治权，并造成了恐惧气氛。当局坚称这是维持稳定所必需的。 除其他外，该法律将任何被视为分裂国家或脱离中国的行为定为犯罪；颠覆;恐怖主义;以及与外国或外部势力勾结。

summary.en: A travel industry group said a new tourism services tax could create problems even for travellers who have already paid in full.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Fijian government will introduce a new tourism services tax for large-scale tourism operators next month, with travel industry experts warning that the costs could be passed on to customers.

The 5 per cent tax will apply from 1 September. The change has been criticised by travel associations in Fiji, Australia and New Zealand, who claim they were not properly consulted.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) said the measure could catch out travellers who have already booked trips to Fiji from September onward, as travel agents and operators face confusion over how to administer the tax.

"The design and roll out reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," ATIA CEO Dean Long said.

"Travellers are the ones left exposed. Families with September school holiday bookings already paid in full, and travellers on large group, corporate and film production bookings, are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago. That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith."

The change forms part of wider taxation amendments enacted as part of Fiji's 2026-2027 national budget, passed last month.

It will affect tourism operators — including hotel, tourism and cruise businesses — with an annual turnover above FJ$2 million (approximately $1.3 million).

According to Fijian finance minister Esrom Immanuel, revenue from the tax will be used to support Fiji Airways.

"The revenue generated will be ring-fenced and fully directed to Fiji Airways, which continues to face financial pressure from rising aviation fuel costs and its ongoing recovery from losses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic," Immanuel told local media in June.

It's reported that the tourism tax will generate around FJ$70 million ($44.7 million) for the airline. The Fijian government is the largest shareholder of Fiji Airways.

ATIA confirmed it will meet with the Fijian government to discuss the tourism services tax, which it said arrived with "zero consultation".

Long said there is ongoing confusion over how the tax is collected, saying that members of the travel industry in Australia and New Zealand — which represent Fiji's largest tourism markets — were not consulted on the change.

"None of this needed to happen. The tax arrived with zero consultation with the travel industry in Australia or New Zealand despite the significant importance of these markets to Fiji," he said.

title.en: Bali jails Swiss tourist for insulting sacred Day of Silence
title.zh: 巴厘岛因侮辱神圣的沉默日而入狱瑞士游客

summary.en: The 26-year-old sparked anger with an expletive-laden post about the sacred holiday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A Swiss tourist has been sentenced to one year in prison for insulting a sacred religious event on Indonesia's holiday island of Bali.

In a now-removed video, Luzian Andrin Zgraggen, 26, had filmed himself walking to an empty beach during the Hindu holiday of Nyepi, describing the scene as "crazy".

He was arrested in March after the video sparked widespread anger among Balinese on social media.

Nyepi, also known as the Day of Silence, is an annual holiday during which the usually bustling tourist island goes quiet, as people stay home and refrain from making loud noises. The restrictions apply to everyone on the island regardless of religion, including tourists.

Entertainment events are restricted and even the use of electricity is discouraged.

Residents typically stock up on groceries ahead of Nyepi so they can stay at home during the holiday.

On Nyepi, which fell on 19 March this year, Zgraggen filmed himself breaking the ban on going out, in an Instagram post captioned with expletives, local media reported.

"What the defendant did offended the Balinese people, hurt their faith and provoked public outrage," the presiding judge said, according to the Associated Press.

Zgraggen said during his trial that he did not understand the extent of Nyepi restrictions and did not mean to insult the Balinese.

"I deeply regret what I did, I apologise to the Balinese people," the Associated Press reported him as saying in court.

Tourists have previously been detained or deported for violating Nyepi restrictions.

Bali has seen tourist numbers recover past its pandemic lull. Last year it welcomed a record seven million international visitors.

But along with the surge in tourism comes misbehaviour that has vexed locals and Balinese authorities. Foreigners have been penalised for offensive acts at religious sites, forming exclusive tourist enclaves and flouting traffic laws .

Authorities have vowed to tighten scrutiny of the island's tourists and crackdown on unruly foreigners.

title.en: US sanctions more Cuban companies and officials
title.zh: 美国制裁更多古巴公司和官员

summary.en: The United States has imposed new sanctions on additional Cuban entities and officials, including an international socialist institute and Cuba's construction ministry, as announced by Marco Rubio.
summary.zh: 据马可·卢比奥宣布，美国对更多古巴公司和官员实施了最新制裁，其中包括一家国际社会主义机构和古巴建设部。

body.en:
The US has imposed a new round of sanctions on Cuban officials and companies, Secretary of State Marco Rubio says.

Nine state-owned mining, metal and building firms, the Ministry of Construction and officials connected to a Cuban-based international institute have been named in the latest tranche of economic sanctions.

In a statement, Rubio accused various figures of "ferrying a new brigade of international sympathizers to Havana to network with regime officials" to coincide with the late former leader Fidel Castro's 100th birthday.

Rubio said the figures targeted by the sanctions form "part of the regime's raison d'être of exporting Marxism, racial resentment, and Communist violence across the world".

Rubio continued: "Today's designations make clear that the Trump Administration will not tolerate the Cuban regime's efforts to fund its repression or continue its decades-long campaign of subversive anti-American activities."

The leadership of the Cuban Institute of Friendship with the Peoples (ICAP) were targeted in the latest round of US sanctions.

Founded in 1960 by Castro, the ICAP has traditionally been used by the Cuban government to foster ties with like-minded organisations around the world by hosting visiting groups of activists who also promote pro-Cuban government campaigns in their own countries.

Rubio, however, accuses the group of "misleading and corrupting American citizens with lies, spy tradecraft and malfeasance".

Among those to be targeted is the group's president, Fernando Gonzalez Llort, a member of a spy ring called the Cuban 5, who were part of a prisoner exchange during the Obama-era thaw with Havana.

Havana's senior figures across the energy, financial and defence sectors are already subject to US sanctions. The country's tourism industry has also plummeted, a key source of income for the beleaguered government.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez condemned Rubio's announcement, writing on X that he was trying to "punish" Cuban companies and further "harm" the economy.

Rodríguez added it would prevent the government "from guaranteeing basic services to the population, which are already in a critical situation as a result of the blockade".

The US has imposed an effective oil blockade on Cuba since the beginning of the year. With the island's aging electricity infrastructure heavily reliant on fuel imports, hospitals have resorted to using emergency generators.

Lengthy and frequent power cuts have triggered rare protests in Cuba, where public dissent is typically punished with long prison sentences.
body.zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥表示，美国对古巴官员和企业实施了新一轮制裁。 九家国有采矿、金属和建筑公司、建设部以及与一家总部位于古巴的国际机构有关的官员已被列入最新一批经济制裁名单。 卢比奥在一份声明中指责多位人士“将一批新的国际同情者运送到哈瓦那，与政权官员建立联系”，以配合已故前领导人菲德尔·卡斯特罗的百岁生日。 卢比奥表示，制裁的对象是“该政权向世界各地输出马克思主义、种族怨恨和共产主义暴力的存在理由的一部分”。 卢比奥继续说道：“今天的指定明确表明，特朗普政府不会容忍古巴政权为其镇压提供资金的努力，也不会继续其长达数十年的颠覆性反美活动。” 古巴人民友好研究所（ICAP）的领导层成为美国最新一轮制裁的目标。 ICAP 由卡斯特罗于 1960 年创立，传统上被古巴政府用来通过接待来访的活动人士团体来促进与世界各地志同道合的组织的联系，这些活动人士也在自己的国家推动亲古巴政府的运动。 然而，卢比奥指责该组织“通过谎言、间谍活动和渎职行为误导和腐蚀美国公民”。 成为目标的人包括该组织的主席费尔南多·冈萨雷斯·略尔特（Fernando Gonzalez Llort），他是一个名为“古巴五人组”的间谍团伙的成员，在奥巴马时代与哈瓦那解冻期间参与了囚犯交换。 哈瓦那能源、金融和国防部门的高级人物已经受到美国的制裁。该国的旅游业也大幅下滑，而旅游业是陷入困境的政府的主要收入来源。 古巴外交部长布鲁诺·罗德里格斯谴责卢比奥的声明，并在X上写道，他试图“惩罚”古巴公司并进一步“损害”经济。 罗德里格斯补充说，这将阻止政府“保证为民众提供基本服务，因为封锁，民众已经处于危急境地”。 今年以来，美国对古巴实施有效的石油封锁。由于岛上老化的电力基础设施严重依赖燃料进口，医院不得不使用应急发电机。 长时间且频繁的断电在古巴引发了罕见的抗议活动，公众异议通常会被判处长期监禁。

title.en: El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office
title.zh: 英国气象局表示，厄尔尼诺现象将是“人们记忆中最强的一次”

summary.en: Scientists say the growing El Niño weather pattern is an "unprecedented event" and means 2027 is likely to be the world's hottest year on record.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The El Niño event that is developing over the Pacific Ocean is likely to be the strongest in living memory, the Met Office has warned.

The powerful natural climate phenomenon pushes up global temperatures and can increase the risks of extreme weather.

Added to the effects of human-induced climate change, the Met Office is warning that it is "very likely" to mean 2027 is the hottest year on record.

There is growing evidence that weather patterns around the world are already being affected, with below-average monsoon rains in India and suppressed hurricane activity in the Atlantic Ocean.

"We should be clear that this is an unprecedented event", said Prof Adam Scaife, head of long-range forecasting at the UK Met Office.

El Niño is a naturally occurring weather pattern, which happens about every two to seven years, lasting for around a year.

Trade winds that typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean can weaken or even reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.

Heat is released from the ocean into the atmosphere, lifting global temperatures and shifting rainfall patterns.

Scientists declare an El Niño when sea surface temperatures in a key area of the Pacific are 0.5C or more above average.

Latest forecasts from the Met Office suggest that these temperature anomalies could exceed 3C later this year as El Niño nears its peak.

This would be unprecedented in records going back to 1950, and probably the strongest event since the 19th century.

Very high temperatures in the deeper ocean - around 8C above normal at a depth of 100m (330ft) in some places - could help to supercharge this El Niño, essentially providing a reservoir of warm water fuel to reinforce the event.

"We have many months to go while this event continues to develop and that's one of the reasons that we have increased confidence that this will be a record-setting event," said Dr Zeke Hausfather, a climate scientist at Berkeley Earth, a US research group.

Some other climate groups have projected something even stronger than the Met Office's forecast, perhaps even 4C above average.

If that came to pass, "It's not beyond the realm of possibility to say this might be the strongest El Niño event in 500 or even 1,000 years," Hausfather said, although it is impossible to say for sure that far back in time.

The change in the distribution of heat across the ocean - and shifts in the wind patterns in the atmosphere above - can have wide ranging effects on the weather right across the globe.

No two El Niño events are the same and the impacts on weather patterns can vary. However, there is evidence that the effects are already being felt.

body.zh: 英国气象局警告说，太平洋上空正在发生的厄尔尼诺现象可能是人们记忆中最强烈的一次。 强大的自然气候现象会推高全球气温，并可能增加极端天气的风险。 除了人为引起的气候变化的影响外，英国气象局警告称，2027 年“很可能”是有记录以来最热的一年。 越来越多的证据表明，世界各地的天气模式已经受到影响，印度的季风降雨量低于平均水平，大西洋的飓风活动受到抑制。 英国气象局长期预报主管亚当·斯凯夫教授表示：“我们应该清楚，这是一次前所未有的事件。” 厄尔尼诺现象是一种自然发生的天气模式，大约每两到七年发生一次，持续一年左右。 通常从东向西吹过太平洋的信风可能会减弱甚至逆转，从而使温暖的海水向东扩散。 热量从海洋释放到大气中，导致全球气温升高并改变降雨模式。 当太平洋主要区域的海面温度比平均水平高出 0.5 摄氏度或以上时，科学家们就会宣布厄尔尼诺现象发生。 英国气象局的最新预测表明，随着厄尔尼诺现象接近峰值，今年晚些时候这些温度异常可能会超过 3 摄氏度。 这在 1950 年以来的记录中是前所未有的，也可能是 19 世纪以来最强烈的事件。 深海中的极高温度——在某些地方100m（330ft）深度处比正常温度高出约8℃——可能有助于加剧厄尔尼诺现象，本质上是提供了一个温水燃料库来强化这一事件。 美国研究小组伯克利地球的气候科学家泽克·豪斯法瑟博士说：“这一事件还需要几个月的时间才能继续发展，这也是我们更有信心这将是一次创纪录事件的原因之一。” 其他一些气候组织的预测甚至比英国气象局的预测还要高，甚至可能比平均水平高 4 摄氏度。 豪斯法瑟说，如果这种情况成为现实，“可以说这可能是 500 年甚至 1000 年来最强烈的厄尔尼诺事件”，尽管不可能确定那么久远的时间。 海洋热量分布的变化以及上方大气风型的变化会对全球天气产生广泛的影响。 没有两次厄尔尼诺事件是相同的，对天气模式的影响也可能有所不同。然而，有证据表明，人们已经感受到了影响。 例如，在厄尔尼诺现象年份，西南季风可能会抑制南亚的降雨量，而到 2026 年为止，...

title.en: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction
title.zh: 为什么尼日利亚曾经的政治巨人可能面临灭绝

summary.en: Once a giant of African politics, the PDP is in danger of being wiped out after January's elections.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Once the undisputed giant of Nigerian politics, the Peoples Democratic Party now finds itself on the brink of extinction.

A question hanging over the campaign for January's general election, which officially kicked off this week, is whether the PDP can survive.

A factional struggle that has ended up in the courts over who exactly is in charge could end up rendering it irrelevant at the ballot box.

It is a remarkable fall for the party, founded in 1998, which appeared impregnable after the end of military rule a year later - so much so that its chairman boasted in 2008 that it would govern for six decades.

For 16 years, it controlled the presidency - in the shape of Olusegun Obasanjo, Umaru Musa Yar'Adua and then Goodluck Jonathan - and the vast majority of the country's 36 states.

The PDP lost the presidential vote to Muhammadu Buhari and the newly formed All Progressives Congress (APC) - a coalition of opposition parties and disgruntled former members.

Thrust into the political wilderness the party's national leaders were bewildered - familiar with the trappings of federal power they had to work out what to do in opposition.

"They were a party that was so used to power, being in opposition was a new challenge they struggled with from the start," he told the BBC.

If 2015 was a major blow, 2025 was the year the party's foundations were left in ruins.

A group of state governors switched party allegiance, which had a particularly devastating effect.

At the start of that year, the PDP still held eight states. But by December, five state governors - from Delta, Akwa Ibom, Enugu, Bayelsa and Rivers - had gone over to the ruling APC.

They cited the PDP's declining viability and a desire for better co-operation with the federal government as reasons for their departure.

Early this year, the PDP held three states but that is now down to zero - with the Oyo governorship slipping from the party's hands just last month.

Internal power struggles, factionalism, insistence that power rotates through the regions and disciplinary measures have all added to the sense of disillusionment within the party.

The PDP has been robbed of high-profile figures and talent, including the loss of former Vice-President Atiku Aubakar last year.

Türkiye, Egypt and Qatar, which have been trying to ‌mediate an end to the Gaza Strip conflict, have condemned recent Israeli strikes in the ‌Palestinian enclave, urging Israel to meet its ceasefire obligations and avoid steps that could ‌escalate tension.

United States envoy Jared Kushner wrapped up a regional visit ‌on Monday amid attempts to advance US President ⁠Donald Trump's plan to end the war.

The international community and Trump's Board of Peace, which is ⁠overseeing the ceasefire, must take ‌the necessary steps to ensure compliance and prevent further escalation, they added.

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 二十年后，中国正在准备迄今为止最大胆的月球任务

summary.en: China's ambitious space program will take it to the moon as soon as next month, and it's looking for water.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

title.en: Why is Israel's military presence growing in Syria?

summary.en: The recent Israeli attack on a Syrian airbase is just one of many Israeli incursions into Syria. In southern Syria, locals say Israeli troops have detained them, destroyed infrastructure and set up military bases.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The recent Israeli attack on a Syrian airbase is just one of many Israeli incursions into Syria. In southern Syria, locals say Israeli troops have detained them, destroyed infrastructure and set up military bases.

It's been two years, four months, 24 days and five hours, said Syrian man Ahmad Hassan al-Din when asked how long it's been since he last saw his son.

In April 2024, Israeli soldiers took Saddam, who had just turned 17, from farmland near the Golan Heights, a part of Syria Israel has occupied since 1967.

"Saddam had gone to feed the animals early in the morning," al-Din, who's from the village of Jubata al-Khashab in the Quneitra district near Golan, told DW. "I called him on the phone, and he told me, 'Everything's fine.' But then later we saw with our own eyes how they took the boy, handcuffed and shackled."

Al-Din filmed Israeli soldiers marching his son through fields. The video, which he forwarded to DW, has previously been verified by open-source investigators at France24 and by human rights organizations.

"They said they took him because he was trespassing on the territory of the state of Israel," al-Din continued. "Even though that area is our farmland and we have a valid UN permit to work there."

To enter this buffer area, Syrian farmers and shepherds needed a special pass from the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force, or UNDOF. The latter was set up to make sure Israeli and Syrian forces kept their distance after a 1974 disengagement agreement.

Humanitarian organizations have since discovered Saddam, now 19, is likely in a prison in Israel.

DW asked the Israeli military what Saddam had been charged with and under which legal system, and a spokesperson said they would investigate. At the time of writing, there had been no further response. 

Since Saddam was taken, the Syrian teenager's story has become one of many similar accounts in this part of southern Syria .

After the fall of the country's dictatorial Assad regime in December 2024, Israel took control of the UN-patrolled demilitarized zone. Senior Israeli politicians declared the 1974 agreement void and said troops would be in the area temporarily to protect Israel from cross-border attacks.

However, since then Israel's presence in Syria has become more permanent. In November 2025, UNDOF told reporters Israel had set up 10 bases in the area. From these bases, Israeli soldiers are making near-daily incursions into the Syrian provinces of Daraa and Quneitra.

title.en: Drought in Germany and Europe are driving up costs
title.zh: 德国和欧洲的干旱导致成本上升

summary.en: Ongoing drought in Europe is causing rivers to dry up and crops to fail. Transport costs are rising and the price of food has exploded. Is inflation due to extreme weather?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ongoing drought in Europe is causing rivers to dry up and crops to fail. Transport costs are rising and the price of food has exploded. Is inflation due to extreme weather?

So far, research institutes have not been able to quantify the impact of extreme weather conditions on inflation in Germany, but there are clear trends.

"If ships on the Rhine can only carry a fraction of their usual cargo, transport costs per metric ton will rise significantly," Torsten Schmidt, an economist at the RWI – Leibniz Institute for Economic Research, told DW.

He added that this would drive up the cost of energy sources, such as diesel and heating oil, which are in large part transported by water. He said that higher costs would be passed on to consumers.

For its data, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) takes into account the effects of global warming, extreme weather and crop losses.

According to the FAO, food prices are currently about 30% higher than in 2020, with meat and oilseeds rising sharply since then.

Recent studies also suggest that climate change and extreme weather events are affecting inflation rates, as are supply bottlenecks as well as gas and oil price shocks caused by the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars.

A study conducted by the European Central Bank (ECB) and five European research institutes entitled "Climate extremes, food price spikes, and their wider societal risks" that was published in July 2025, warned against escalating inflation.

"Central bank mandates for price stability may become increasingly challenging to deliver if more frequent extreme weather events make food prices less stable domestically and in global markets," the study states.

These challenges could become even more trying if temperature rises have a long-term effect on inflation. If inflation has to be dealt with by higher interest rates, economic growth will also be hampered.

In 2023, the ECB published a study called "The asymmetric effects of weather shocks on euro area inflation" that reached a similar conclusion after examining the four largest European Union economies.

"With a changing climate implying an increased frequency and severity of extremes in Europe, the shocks studied here can be expected to occur more frequently and could lead to persistent upward pressures on inflation, especially from extreme temperatures in summer," it read. "Given the differing impacts of shocks in different seasons and across countries, our results also suggest that climate change could enhance heterogeneity of inflation developments across euro area countries."

title.en: How do teenagers keep accessing guns in Southeast Asia?
title.zh: 东南亚青少年如何持续获得枪支？

summary.en: Recent deadly shootings involving teenagers in Thailand and the Philippines have brought gun laws under scrutiny. The incidents raise concerns about broader issues of firearm access, accountability, and enforcement in Southeast Asia.
summary.zh: 泰国和菲律宾近期发生的涉及青少年的致命枪击事件，使枪支法律受到严格审查。这些事件引发了人们对东南亚枪支获取、问责制和执法方面更广泛问题的担忧。

body.en:
Recent deadly shootings in Thailand and the Philippines have put gun laws under scrutiny while raising questions about a broader problem of firearm access, accountability and enforcement.

On August 7, a 14-year-old Thai student killed his grandparents before taking his grandfather's handgun to his school outside Bangkok and killing five teachers and staff members and a 12-year-old student. The attacker then turned the weapon on himself.

Police said the teenager fired at least 26 rounds during the attack, Thailand's deadliest mass killing in almost four years.

This week, another school shooting occurred in the southern Philippine city of Zamboanga, when a ninth-grade student killed another pupil and later died by suicide. Police said one of the weapons belonged to his father, a customs police official.

The attacks raise questions not only about Thailand and the Philippines' unusually large civilian gun stockpile, but also about how legally owned firearms are stored, transferred and allowed to fall into other people's hands across Southeast Asia.

The Small Arms Survey estimated in 2017 that Thai civilians possessed around 10.3 million firearms, equivalent to roughly 15 guns for every 100 people, by far the highest rate in Southeast Asia. Just over 6 million were registered, leaving more than 4 million unregistered.

The Philippines rivals Thailand, with several million firearms believed to be in civilian hands and a comparatively high rate of firearm killings, although fewer per capita than in Thailand. Malaysia has fewer than one civilian gun for every 100 people, while Indonesia's rate is lower still.

Thailand's estimated firearm death rate of 3.49 per 100,000 people is one of the highest in Asia, according to the World Population Review.

Thailand has experienced a succession of high-profile attacks in recent years, including a  school shooting in southern Thailand this February.

In 2020, nearly 30 people were killed   by a gunman at a shopping mall in the northern city of Nakhon Ratchasima. In 2022,  a massacre at a childcare center  left 37 people dead. A shooting at a Bangkok shopping mall in 2023 led to calls for tighter gun laws.  

At first glance, Thailand's laws appear restrictive. Separate authorization is required to purchase, possess and carry a firearm, and there are several layers of registration for legal firearms.

Yet possession licences remain valid for life, applicants are not subjected to mental-health screenings, and licence holders are not periodically reassessed.

title.en: Bangladesh lawmakers elect BNP's Alamgir as president
title.zh: 孟加拉国议员选举民族主义党阿拉姆吉尔为总统

summary.en: Lawmakers in Bangladesh have elected a longtime opposition figure, Alamgir of the BNP party, as president. His party came to power following a 2024 revolution that led to the ousting of the previous government led by Sheikh Hasina.
summary.zh: 孟加拉国议员选举长期反对派人物、民族主义党（BNP）的阿拉姆吉尔为总统。他的政党是在2024年推翻谢赫·哈西娜政府的革命后上台的。

body.en:
The longtime opposition figure's party came to power after the 2024 revolution, which ousted the government of Sheikh Hasina.

Bangladesh's  Parliament elected ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the country's new president on Thursday.

The BNP, which holds more than a two-thirds majority in parliament, secured the largely ceremonial post for Alamgir, defeating retired army officer-turned-politician Oli Ahmed of the opposition Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance.

Alamgir won with 255 votes to Oli's 88 to become the 23rd president of the country of 173 million.

It was the first contested presidential election since 1991, when Bangladesh became a parliamentary democracy.

The vote comes after former president Mohammed Shahabuddin, a close ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina , resigned last month citing health concerns.

"I dream of a happy, prosperous, and welfare-oriented state where marginalized communities, hard-working people, and daily wage earners can afford meals twice a day," Alamgir, 78, said Thursday before the vote, according to the state news agency BSS.

His challenger, 87-year-old Oli, said the country had "high hopes" for his presidency.

"We expect you to serve the country by putting national interests above personal interests," he said after the vote.

Bangladesh's close ally China congratulated Alamgir, saying it looked forward to "a shared future in the new era," its high commission in the capital, Dhaka, said in a statement.

In February, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's BNP won a landslide victory in the first election since Hasina's 2024 ouster.

Hasina remains in exile in India. She was found guilty in absentia in November of crimes against humanity and sentenced to be hanged. Rights groups say her rule was marked by widespread abuses, including the murder of rivals and supression of political opposition.

Born in 1948, Alamgir entered politics while studying economics at Dhaka University. He was a key student leader in the 1969 uprising opposing military rule by Pakistan, before becoming an economics teacher. He joined the BNP in the early 1990s and rose steadily through its ranks.

He became well known nationally as an opposition leader during Hasina's 15-year rule and was repeatedly arrested under her government, facing dozens of charges he said were politically motivated.

Alamgir has been hailed in the media for "keeping the BNP organized and maintaining the party's political presence during difficult times," referring to Hasina's rule. 

As president, he will serve as the head of state and commander-in-chief of the armed forces. He is expected to be sworn in on Friday evening.

body.en:
Six years after stepping down as working royals, Prince Harry and his wife Meghan Markle are moving back to the United Kingdom within weeks, British press reported on Thursday.

In a surprise move, Harry, the youngest son of King Charles III, and his wife "plan to leave the United States by the end of the month to settle in a private, non-royal residence, which is said to be located outside London", The Telegraph reported.

Several UK news outlets, including the BBC, reported the couple's two children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, had already been enrolled in a British school for the start of the school year in early September.

It was reported that the couple had already chosen a new house, but that it would not be one of the many royal residences.

Harry and Meghan have lived in California since stepping down as working royals in 2020 and the children had not seen their grandfather Charles since 2022.

Harry, 41, and Meghan, 45, left the UK for North America in 2020 amid a bitter feud with his family, which worsened as Harry published his tell-all memoir Spare.

A no-holds-barred interview with US talk show host Oprah Winfrey also deepened the rift.

The BBC said the 77-year-old Charles had been made aware on Sunday that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex planned to return to live in the UK.

The monarch welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private and personal capacity, but there will be no expected change to the couple's official status, the BBC reported.

While no official reason for the move has been shared, the news comes only weeks after Harry and Meghan paid a short visit to the UK in early July with the children, during which they had a private meeting with Charles.

Harry said last year that he wanted to reconcile with his father, who was diagnosed two years ago with cancer and has been receiving treatment since. The type of cancer has never been revealed.

It was not immediately clear whether Harry's older brother and heir to the throne, Prince William, and his wife, Catherine, had been told of the news. The two brothers have become estranged and reportedly no longer talk.

The UK's Sun newspaper reported the couple would keep their Montecito home in California.

While the couple signed a mega deal with Netflix in 2020 — reportedly worth an unconfirmed US$100 million ($140 million) — many of their projects have struggled to win over audiences.

title.en: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists guilty in national security trial
title.zh: 香港天安门活动人士在国家安全审判中被判有罪

summary.en: Three activists were accused of inciting others to subvert state power under the China-introduced law.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under the city's controversial national security law.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail after being convicted under the China-introduced law. Sentencing is expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", according to a summary on Friday. Chow told the court in May the law itself was on trial.

Hong Kong used to be one of the only places in Chinese territory where people could gather to mark the deadly 1989 crackdown against pro-democracy protesters.

Authorities banned these gatherings in 2020, citing Covid-19 policies, but they have never resumed. This was also the year the national security law, which makes illegal a wider range of dissenting acts, officially came into force.

In mainland China, authorities have banned even oblique references to the 1989 crackdown.

The HKA was founded in May 1989 to support students holding pro-democracy rallies. Weeks later, the Communist Party crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square with troops and tanks. Estimates of the death toll range from a few hundred to many thousands.

Over the next three decades, HKA called on authorities to accept responsibility for the crackdown, free dissidents and introduce democratic reform.

Rights group Amnesty International has said the case "relies on vague, overly broad and arbitrary definitions of 'subversion'".

Sarah Brooks, Amnesty International's Deputy Regional Director, said Chow and Lee had "not committed any recognisable crime".

"Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan are prisoners of conscience who should never have been prosecuted in the first place. They must be released immediately and unconditionally", she added.

In a separate case, Chow was arrested in June 2021 for "inciting" the public to take part in that year's vigil and later found guilty.

However, Hong Kong's top court overturned that conviction in 2022 , with a judge ruling the police hadn't properly justified the vigil's ban.

Chow Hang-tung spoke to the BBC in 2021, weeks before her arrest on 4 June 2022.

Critics say the national security law has eroded Hong Kong's autonomy and created a climate of fear. Authorities insist it is needed to maintain stability.

Among other things, the law criminalises anything considered as secession, or breaking away from China; subversion; terrorism; and collusion with foreign or external forces.
body.zh: 根据香港备受争议的国家安全法，两名组织年度守夜活动纪念 1989 年天安门广场镇压活动的香港活动人士被判犯有煽动他人颠覆国家政权罪。 根据中国出台的法律，69岁的李卓人和41岁的周恒东被定罪，最高可判处10年监禁。预计将在晚些时候宣判。 根据周五的摘要，李和周“煽动他人以非法手段组织、策划、实施或者参与行为，以颠覆国家政权”。周五月份告诉法庭，该法律本身正在接受审判。 香港曾经是中国境内唯一一个人们可以聚集纪念1989年镇压亲民主抗议者的地方。 当局以 Covid-19 政策为由，在 2020 年禁止了这些聚会，但从未恢复。今年也是《国家安全法》正式生效的一年，该法将范围更广的异议行为定为非法。 在中国大陆，当局甚至禁止间接提及 1989 年的镇压行动。 香港学生会成立于1989年5月，旨在支持学生举行民主集会。几周后，共产党用军队和坦克镇压了北京天安门广场的民主抗议活动。死亡人数估计从数百人到数千人不等。 在接下来的三十年里，香港协会呼吁当局承担镇压责任，释放异见人士并推行民主改革。 人权组织国际特赦组织表示，此案“依赖于‘颠覆’的模糊、过于宽泛和武断的定义”。 国际特赦组织区域副主任萨拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 表示，周和李“没有犯下任何可识别的罪行”。 她补充说：“周恒东和李卓人是良心犯，本来就不应该受到起诉。必须立即无条件释放他们。” 在另一起案件中，周先生于 2021 年 6 月因“煽动”公众参加当年的守夜活动而被捕，后来被判有罪。 然而，香港最高法院于 2022 年推翻了这一判决，法官裁定警方没有适当证明禁止守夜活动的合理性。 周恒东于 2021 年接受 BBC 采访，几周后她于 2022 年 6 月 4 日被捕。 批评人士称，国家安全法削弱了香港的自治权，并造成了恐惧气氛。当局坚称这是维持稳定所必需的。 除其他外，该法律将任何被视为分裂国家或脱离中国的行为定为犯罪；颠覆;恐怖主义;以及与外国或外部势力勾结。

title.en: Hong Kong convicts activists in national security trial

summary.en: The two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists were found guilty of inciting subversion. The high profile case has been widely criticized for highlighting the deterioration of freedom of expression.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists were found guilty of inciting subversion. The high profile case has been widely criticized for highlighting the deterioration of freedom of expression.

A Hong Kong court on Thursday convicted two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists tried under Beijing's  controversial national security law for "incitement to subversion."

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, had organized candlelight vigils to mark Beijing's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. They were charged in 2021 and both pleaded not guilty.

They face a maximum prison term of 10 years and are expected to be sentenced at a later date.

The pair "incited other persons to organize, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", a press summary handed out to reporters said.

Prosecutors had argued they "endanger(ed) national security in the name of human rights."

Public commemoration of the deadly Tiananmen crackdown , when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital's Tiananmen Square, have been effectively banned since the 2020 imposition of the national security law on Hong Kong.

The controversial law came after Hong Kong's 2019 massive anti-government, pro-democracy protests.

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 二十年后，中国正在准备迄今为止最大胆的月球任务

summary.en: China's ambitious space program will take it to the moon as soon as next month, and it's looking for water.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

title.en: Founder of collapsed Chinese property giant Evergrande sentenced to life in prison
title.zh: 中国倒闭房地产巨头恒大创始人被判无期徒刑

summary.en: The founder of the collapsed Chinese property giant Evergrande has been sentenced to life in prison, marking a significant development in the aftermath of the company's failure, which severely impacted China's real estate sector.
summary.zh: 中国恒大地产集团的创始人因公司倒闭而被判处无期徒刑，这标志着恒大危机余波中的一个关键时刻，该危机曾震动了中国的房地产行业。

body.en:
The founder of Evergrande, the property giant at the centre of China's housing market slump, has been sentenced to life in prison and had all of his personal property confiscated.

Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty in April to several charges, including embezzlement of assets and corporate bribery.

Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court also fined his former companies a total of 15.82bn yuan (£1.73bn; $2.35bn) over multiple crimes, including falsifying records and concealing debt.

Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector and hit investors and domestic banks hard.

Hui and his businesses "seriously disrupted" the Chinese property market, resulting in significant economic losses, the court said.

Other Evergrande executives, including Hui's two sons Xu Zhijian and Xu Tenghe, were also sentenced to jail terms ranging from 22 months to 18 years, according to state media.

Once ranked Asia's richest man, Hui has seen his wealth and influence dwindle as his company unravelled.

Hui, also known as Xu Jiayin, rose from humble beginnings in rural China, where he was raised by his grandmother before venturing into property development and setting up Evergrande in 1996.

He oversaw the company's rapid rise through an aggressive expansion programme funded with large amounts of borrowed money.

Evergrande became China's biggest real estate developer, with a stock market valuation of more than $50bn (£36.7bn). Hui was once estimated to be Asia's richest person .

The firm was dealt a huge blow when Beijing introduced measures in 2020 to control debt in the country's property sector.

As the company struggled to meet interest payments on its debts it sold properties at huge discounts to stay afloat before collapsing in 2021.

In April, the court heard that the company had taken millions of dollars in pre-sale funding from potential house buyers that were not used for construction.

The money had instead been channelled to new property developments, resulting in hundreds of unfinished projects.

In March 2024, Hui was fined $6.5m and banned from China's capital market for life for his company overstating its revenue by $78bn .

Evergrande's stock market valuation shrank by 99% before its shares were removed from the Hong Kong exchange in August 2025 after more than a decade and a half of trading.

Evergrande's implosion has often been blamed for triggering a broader slump in China's property market that continues to weigh heavily on the economy.

At its height, Evergrande was the biggest firm in the country's real estate industry, which made up about a third of China's gross domestic product at the time.

body.zh: 处于中国房地产市场低迷之中的房地产巨头恒大集团的创始人被判处无期徒刑，并被没收全部个人财产。 许家印四月份承认多项指控，包括贪污资产和企业贿赂。 深圳市中级人民法院还因伪造记录和隐瞒债务等多项罪行，对他以前的公司处以人民币 158.2 亿元（17.3 亿英镑；23.5 亿美元）的罚款。 许的判决标志着恒大倒闭影响的关键时刻，恒大倒闭震动了中国房地产行业，并对投资者和国内银行造成了沉重打击。 法院表示，许先生及其企业“严重扰乱”中国房地产市场，造成重大经济损失。 据官方媒体报道，恒大的其他高管，包括许志坚的两个儿子徐志坚和徐腾鹤，也被判处 22 个月至 18 年不等的监禁。 曾一度被评为亚洲首富的许氏眼睁睁地看着自己的财富和影响力随着公司的解体而逐渐减少。 许家印在中国农村出身卑微，由祖母抚养长大，随后开始涉足房地产开发，并于 1996 年创立恒大集团。 他通过利用大量借来的资金进行积极的扩张计划，见证了公司的快速崛起。 恒大成为中国最大的房地产开发商，股票市场估值超过 500 亿美元（367 亿英镑）。许氏一度被估计为亚洲首富。 当北京于2020年推出控制中国房地产行业债务的措施时，该公司遭受了巨大打击。 由于该公司难以支付债务利息，因此在 2021 年倒闭之前以大幅折扣出售了房产以维持运营。 4月份，法院获悉该公司从潜在购房者那里收取了数百万美元的预售资金，但这些资金并未用于建设。 这笔钱反而被用于新的房地产开发，导致数百个未完工的项目。 2024年3月，许先生因其公司虚报收入780亿美元而被罚款650万美元，并终身禁止进入中国资本市场。 经过十五年多的交易后，恒大股份于 2025 年 8 月从香港交易所退市之前，其股票市场估值缩水了 99%。 恒大的内爆常常被指责引发中国房地产市场更广泛的衰退，继续给经济带来沉重压力。 在鼎盛时期，恒大是中国房地产行业最大的公司，房地产行业约占当时中国国内生产总值的三分之一。 房地产市场是增长的重要推动力，也是当地的重要收入来源......

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

"Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in...
body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. Indonesia's efforts to navigate its foreign policy amidst regional tensions reflect the ongoing challenge of living at peace with all, as far as it depends on them. This pursuit requires wisdom and a steadfast commitment to de-escalation and understanding.

body.en:
The Fijian government will introduce a new tourism services tax for large-scale tourism operators next month, with travel industry experts warning that the costs could be passed on to customers.

The 5 per cent tax will apply from 1 September. The change has been criticised by travel associations in Fiji, Australia and New Zealand, who claim they were not properly consulted.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) said the measure could catch out travellers who have already booked trips to Fiji from September onward, as travel agents and operators face confusion over how to administer the tax.

"The design and roll out reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," ATIA CEO Dean Long said.

"Travellers are the ones left exposed. Families with September school holiday bookings already paid in full, and travellers on large group, corporate and film production bookings, are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago. That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith."

The change forms part of wider taxation amendments enacted as part of Fiji's 2026-2027 national budget, passed last month.

It will affect tourism operators — including hotel, tourism and cruise businesses — with an annual turnover above FJ$2 million (approximately $1.3 million).

According to Fijian finance minister Esrom Immanuel, revenue from the tax will be used to support Fiji Airways.

"The revenue generated will be ring-fenced and fully directed to Fiji Airways, which continues to face financial pressure from rising aviation fuel costs and its ongoing recovery from losses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic," Immanuel told local media in June.

It's reported that the tourism tax will generate around FJ$70 million ($44.7 million) for the airline. The Fijian government is the largest shareholder of Fiji Airways.

ATIA confirmed it will meet with the Fijian government to discuss the tourism services tax, which it said arrived with "zero consultation".

Long said there is ongoing confusion over how the tax is collected, saying that members of the travel industry in Australia and New Zealand — which represent Fiji's largest tourism markets — were not consulted on the change.

"None of this needed to happen. The tax arrived with zero consultation with the travel industry in Australia or New Zealand despite the significant importance of these markets to Fiji," he said.

title.en: 'House of cards': The uncertain future of addiction help in Australia

summary.en: Half a million Australians are said to be exposed amid "significant uncertainty" about funding for the sector.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Half a million Australians have no access to desperately needed drug and alcohol addiction help, and funding uncertainty is intensifying the risk to existing services, a peak health provider warns.

The Australasian Therapeutic Communities Association (ATCA) fears that funding for many services is "a house of cards" that will collapse if federal funding is cut or not renewed.

ATCA chair Gerard Byrne said its members, who provide residential therapy, outreach and day programs, were reporting increases in waiting lists and waiting times.

"They turn up in hospitals, in police stations, in courts, in prison, in homeless services, in domestic and family violence services," he said.

"But they're not going there for the drug and alcohol problem. They're going there because all of those other things were happening for them because they couldn't get the drug and alcohol service."

ATCA executive officer Michelle Ridley said half a million Australians needing drug and alcohol treatment were missing out, and the issue was most acute in regional and remote areas.

"There is significant uncertainty about future funding for the sector and without confirmation of ongoing funding, some services undoubtedly face very hard decisions about their future admissions," she said.

"Our members are operating in an environment of significant pressure due to increasing demand for alcohol and other drug treatment services, workforce challenges, and uncertainty about future funding arrangements.."

Following a review of the federal Drug and Alcohol Program, the federal government extended existing grants until the end of June 2027.

Byrne said the sector needed the grant opportunities for the next round of three-year grant agreements to be released soon.

"The uncertainty is in what the future will be after the application process, because we're funded up until June 2027, but our members don't know what's happening after that," he said.

"DAP funding usually part funds programs along with the state and territory governments, so you get this house of cards situation where if you take one funding stream away or reduce it, the other funding streams are at risk because the financial sustainability is not there."

The Southern Highlands property market has long attracted Australians seeking a tree-change — but Duncan Hill believes the NSW region has now become a prime buyer's market.

"We're definitely seeing a buying opportunity ... it's probably the best time that I've seen in the last five years," Hill told SBS News.

He founded Duncan Hill Property, based in the Southern Highlands town of Bowral, in 2013. Since then, Hill has witnessed changes to the regional housing market .

"We did see [housing price] growth of about 30 per cent over the last five years, but then it's declined now by about two to three per cent over the last 12 months."

That shift is consistent with Cotality's latest quarterly regional market update, which found Australia's housing market downturn is no longer confined to capital cities.

The update did note that regional markets remained more resilient to change and typically outperformed capital cities.

"A lot of buyers have been pushed out by the affordability pressures and by the increases in interest rates that we've seen so far," Burg told SBS News.

But Burg believes recent rate hikes, compounded by a cost of living crisis , mean "fewer buyers nationally [are] ready to make a purchase".

title.en: Albanese wanted 'full accountability' from Israel. Instead, Australia is 'outraged'
title.zh: 阿尔巴尼斯希望以色列承担“全部责任”。相反，澳大利亚感到“愤怒”

summary.en: Outrage over Israel's response to aid worker Zomi Frankcom's killing is the latest flashpoint in a relationship that's no longer warm.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Israel's decision not to pursue criminal proceedings over the killing of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom has sparked "outrage" from the federal government, signalling a new low for relations between the two countries.

The decision comes after almost three years of increasingly strained ties, with Australia moving from backing Israel after the October 7 attacks to i mposing sanctions on Israeli government ministers and recognising a Palestinian state.

Despite previously conceding there had been "serious failures", the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) on Wednesday announced it would not prosecute those responsible for the death of Frankcom and six of her World Central Kitchen colleagues in an IDF strike in Gaza in April 2024.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision "falls far short of the accountability we expect" in some of her most critical comments against Israel since the Gaza war began.

Asked about Australia's relationship with Israel, Wong said it was facing a "difficult time".

She said the federal government only became aware of the decision moments before it was publicly announced, and it was "especially insulting" to Frankcom's family that it came on World Humanitarian Day, a point echoed by Zomi's brother Mal in a statement.

The Greens called for the Israeli ambassador, Hillel Newman, who was summoned by the government for an explanation on Thursday, to be expelled.

Opposition defence spokesperson James Paterson said the news was "incredibly concerning", but he needed to receive a full briefing before making further comment.

Frankcom and her colleagues were travelling in a marked aid convoy in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, when they were hit by three Israeli drone strikes on 1 April 2024.

The Israeli military initially said the convoy had been mistaken for a group of Hamas fighters before later acknowledging the vehicles had been misidentified and there had been serious failures in the decision-making leading to the attack.

Australia and Israel have historically enjoyed warm relations, with Australia supporting Israel at international forums such as the United Nations.

The Australian government's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade states in a current country briefing on its website that "Australia and Israel share a close relationship with significant people-to-people links and broad commercial engagement."

title.en: Australia's new media bargaining laws put pressure on tech platforms to pay for news
title.zh: 澳大利亚新媒体讨价还价法给科技平台带来支付新闻费用的压力

summary.en: The passage of the News Bargaining laws comes just 24 hours after laws restricting gambling advertisements.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian government passed legislation on Thursday that will force tech giants to pay millions of dollars in levies if they fail to strike commercial deals with local media outlets for news on their platforms.

The News Bargaining Incentive taxes the companies 2.5 per cent on their advertising revenues unless they strike agreements.

Proceeds from the scheme would be directed to local Australian news outlets, whose content helps drive user engagement and advertising revenue on the tech firms' platforms.

The levy applies to Meta, Alphabet's Google, TikTok and Microsoft's LinkedIn, covering companies with a "significant" social media or search service in Australia, and local advertising revenue exceeding $250 million.

Platforms can avoid the charge by reaching agreements with at least eight different publishers by the end of their reporting period. The value of those deals would be offset against their levy liability.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The deals must support the production of news content or relate to news content produced by the publishers being made available online by the platform, the legislation said.

Spending with large publishers carries a 150 per cent offset, while spending with small and medium-sized outlets carries a 200 per cent offset.

"The legislation is here, and the message to platforms to pursue commercial deals is clear. Deals will need to be finalised before the end of a digital platform's financial reporting period to be used to offset their liability in that period," the government said in a statement.

"This is an important day for Australian news businesses and Australian journalism."

The passage of the News Bargaining Incentive comes one day after parliament passed laws restricting gambling advertisements.

title.en: 'Significant escalation': Mass mortality events leave over 1,000 birds dead in South Australia

summary.en: Over 1,000 birds have died in South Australia due to mass mortality events, prompting Premier Peter Malinauskas to express deep concern.

body.en:
Authorities in South Australia have identified three mass mortality bird events. The events involve more than 1,000 crested terns, which authorities "presumed" died of the H5N1 bird flu.

The deaths, detected on Wednesday, occurred on remote islands including Troubridge Island, as well as North Page and South Page close to Kangaroo Island.

State government surveillance teams discovered the dead birds, and are considered a "significant escalation" of bird flu cases in the state, South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas said in an address to the SA parliament.

"The loss of more than 1,000 birds is deeply concerning, and the state government is treating these events with the utmost seriousness," he said.

"Of particular concern, we are also investigating a suspected case involving a little penguin from Kangaroo Island."

Malinauskas said that no similar mortality events had been reported in mammals. He also noted that H5N1 had not yet been detected in any poultry or livestock.

South Australia has recorded 177 confirmed H5 bird flu cases as of Friday 21 August.

reflection.en: The news of mass bird deaths in South Australia reminds us of the fragility of creation and the distress within the natural world. Romans 8:22 speaks of creation groaning, awaiting redemption, a sentiment echoed in the concern over such significant loss of life. It calls us to reflect on our role in stewarding the earth and its creatures.
reflection.zh: 南澳大利亚大量鸟类死亡的消息提醒我们，受造界是脆弱的，自然界也存在着痛苦。罗马书8:22提到受造之物一同叹息，等候得赎，这与人们对如此重大生命损失的担忧不谋而合。它呼吁我们反思自己在管理地球及其生物方面的角色。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
